First-class and higher-order functions
First-class functions as a property of JavaScript, and higher-order functions that take or return functions: map, React HOCs and Vue slots.
Understand the difference between first-class functions, a property of the language, and higher-order functions, which take or return functions, and learn to write your own higher-order functions.
text
Functions in JavaScript are first-class, and that is what makes higher-order functions possible.

First-class functions are a property of the language: in it, functions are values just like numbers or strings. A function can be assigned to a variable, passed as an argument to another function, and returned from a function.
Higher-order functions is the term commonly used for functions that accept other functions as arguments or return a function.
code

In short, a function that takes or returns a function is a higher-order function. "First-class", on the other hand, is not the role a function plays in a call but a property of the language: in JavaScript any function can be passed or returned like an ordinary value.

In React a component is a value (a function or a class), so it can be passed to a function: a higher-order component (HOC) is a function that takes a component and returns a new component. In Vue a component is usually described by an options object rather than a function (only a functional component is a plain function), but the idea is the same: components and slots are passed around as values, and in render functions slots are functions that receive data and return virtual nodes (vnodes).
